assessment.nobel_worthiness: Staggered nominal contracts, Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and the Woodford micro-founded synthesis form the standard framework for analysing monetary policy. They shaped central-bank practice and a large body of macroeconomic research, and the framework explains patterns in the data as well as organising them.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (1983) gave the tractable pricing mechanism. Taylor gave staggered contracts and the policy rule. Woodford gave the unified normative and positive framework. Gali, Gertler, Clarida, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans and Smets made major contributions to estimation and extensions, so a three-person limit leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, with durable influence through the post-2008 and post-2020 inflation episodes. The framework has been tested and revised but not displaced.
uncertainties: The three-name limit excludes Gali, Gertler and the CEE trio, and a different split of credit is defensible.
Post-2021 inflation and the HANK critique may be read as limiting the framework's standing.
My assessment draws on general knowledge, not independent verification of the record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Difference and system GMM estimators for dynamic panels are among the most-used tools in applied microeconomics, macroeconomics and finance. They solved a practical identification problem that applied researchers face constantly, so the methodological impact is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991), Arellano-Bover (1995) and Blundell-Bond (1998) form a coherent core, so the three-person credit is relatively clean. Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin-Newey-Rosen and Hansen's GMM are antecedents, and Hansen is already a laureate.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of use, with well-understood limits such as weak instruments and instrument proliferation. This is a fully mature contribution.
uncertainties: The Committee may regard these as refinements of GMM and panel methods that are already recognised.
Some of the credit may belong to antecedent work.
Known misuse of the estimators in applied papers could temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade model reoriented international trade around firm-level selection, exporter premia and gains from reallocation. It connects theory tightly to micro data and has generated a large empirical literature.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) and Helpman's broader work on firms and trade are closely linked. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are important contributors who are not credited on this ballot entry. Redding's contributions are later and extend the framework.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of validation and extension, with measurement of the gains from trade refined and debated.
uncertainties: Omitting Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum could weaken the attribution.
Helpman may be seen as better credited under other work, such as new trade theory.
The quantitative magnitude of gains is model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work combines the skill-biased and task-based accounts of wage inequality with credible quasi-experimental evidence on import competition. Together the two strands reshaped how economists and policymakers understand labour-demand shocks, adjustment costs and local labour markets. It joins new data, an explanatory framework and credible identification.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task approach and the trade-shock studies. Katz is central to the skill-premium evidence. Hanson is central to the China-shock identification. Dorn and others, including Acemoglu (already a laureate), shared important parts. The three-name limit makes any split contestable.
assessment.maturity: The skill-premium literature dates to the 1990s, and the trade-shock work is over a decade old with extensive replication and debate on magnitudes.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles two strands, and credit between them is hard to apportion.
Size and persistence of the trade shock effects remain debated.
Dorn is excluded despite being a co-author on the key papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a quantifiable, data-based account of how distortions across firms generate large cross-country TFP gaps. It organised a major agenda in growth, development and macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the anchor. Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) is a parallel founding paper, and Rogerson is not credited on this entry. Restuccia is credited, so the choice of two names leaves out an arguably co-equal contributor.
assessment.maturity: Seventeen years of use, though measurement concerns about whether dispersion in revenue productivity reflects distortions or measurement error are substantial.
uncertainties: Measurement error and adjustment costs could explain some measured misallocation.
Restuccia-Rogerson priority complicates the split of credit.
Policy relevance depends on identifying the specific distortions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how econometricians reason about what data can and cannot say without strong assumptions. It reframed credible inference, and it also affects treatment choice and policy analysis. The conceptual contribution is foundational and the influence is wide.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator, starting with the 1989 bounds and his work on the reflection problem and on treatment choice. Tamer and Molinari did important later work on moment inequalities and inference, which is more technical and more recent.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades since the origin, with substantial uptake in applied settings, though adoption is slower than for point-identified approaches.
uncertainties: Applied uptake is narrower than the conceptual influence.
Whether the Committee prefers a single laureate or a group including Tamer and Molinari is unclear.
Econometric theory may be seen as already well represented among recent awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Archival reconstruction of top income shares from tax records created a new empirical foundation for long-run inequality research. It is a clear case of data discovery that shifted the research agenda and public debate. The explanatory framework is less settled than the data, and the theory of the r>g mechanism is contested.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez (2003) is the foundational top-incomes work. Zucman's later work on offshore wealth is substantial but more recent. Atkinson, now deceased, was a major pioneer, so credit is shared with a person who cannot be recognised.
assessment.maturity: Two decades since the core data work, which has been replicated across countries. Wealth-distribution estimates remain contested.
uncertainties: Measurement disputes over wealth concentration and income definitions persist.
Atkinson's priority complicates attribution.
Political salience must not influence the evaluation, and I try to apply scientific criteria only.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The résumé correspondence design of Bertrand and Mullainathan (2004) gave a transparent, credible method for measuring discrimination in hiring. It spurred a very large literature across countries and domains. The method is influential, and the substantive finding is robust.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand-Mullainathan (2004) is the signature study. The audit and correspondence tradition has earlier roots, including in sociology and other economists' work, so credit for the method is shared. Charles is credited here for other work on discrimination, and attribution to him is weaker.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of replication, and later meta-analyses broadly support the findings. Questions about what drives the callback gaps remain open.
uncertainties: Credit for the method is shared with earlier audit-study pioneers.
Callback gaps do not map cleanly onto wage or employment outcomes.
My own research is in a neighbouring area of labour economics, and I flag this as a possible bias in evaluating the field.
